hiphop.summary: Hip-hop is built on the beat: hard drums, a sample or loop, and a bass that locks to the kick, all leaving room for the voice.
hiphop.feel: 4/4 with a slight swing on the 16ths (the MPC feel). The kick plays around the beat; the snare lands hard on 2 and 4.
hiphop.keys: Mostly minor keys. Minor 7th chords and Dorian colour from jazz and soul records.
sounds: Punchy sampled drums: a dusty kick, a cracking snare, crisp hats
A soul, jazz or funk sample (keys, horns, strings) chopped into a loop
A deep, round bass (electric or sub) that follows the kick
Rhodes or Wurlitzer for warm chords
Vinyl crackle and tape saturation for character
drums: Kick on 1 and the 'and' of 2 or 3; snare on 2 and 4
Hats in 8ths with a little swing (about 55-60%)
Ghost snares or rimshots between the hits add bounce
Keep fills short: drop the drums for a bar before the hook
bass: Play the root on the kick hits and rest when the kick rests
Short, round notes sit best; slide into the next root now and then
harmony: Loop two or four chords, often minor 7ths (i7 - iv7, i7 - VI7)
Jazz voicings on keys: add 9ths and 11ths
The loop often never 'resolves': it hypnotises
arrangement: Intro 4-8 bars (the sample alone, or filtered)
Verse 16 bars, hook 8 bars, repeated
Change the drums for the hook (add a clap or open hats)
mix: Kick and bass share the low end: sidechain or EQ them apart
Low-pass the sample under the verse, open it up in the hook
Light tape saturation glues everything together
tips: Pick the sample first, then build the drums around its groove
Leave space for the vocal (1-4 kHz) in the verse

trap.summary: Trap is half-time and heavy: rolling hi-hats, a booming 808 that carries the bass line, and a dark, simple melody on top.
trap.feel: 4/4 in half time: the clap or snare lands on beat 3 of each bar. Hats in 8ths and 16ths with fast rolls and triplets.
trap.keys: Minor keys (natural minor, harmonic minor; Phrygian for an even darker colour). C#, F, G and A minor are common.
sounds: 808: a long, tuned sub bass with a little distortion so it's heard on phones
Crisp hi-hats and a clap or snare with a short tail
Dark bells, plucks or piano for the melody (music box, glockenspiel)
Pads, choirs or strings for atmosphere
FX: risers, reversed cymbals, vocal chops
drums: Clap or snare on beat 3 (half time)
Kick on 1, then syncopated hits that the 808 follows
Hats in 8ths with 1/16, 1/32 and triplet rolls, mostly at the end of phrases
Open hats and percussion on offbeats; drop the drums for a bar before the hook
bass: The 808 is the bass: tune it to the key and play the roots with the kick
Glide (portamento) up or down an octave between notes for movement
Let it ring between hits, and stop it before the next one
harmony: Two to four minor chords: i - VI, or i - VI - III - VII
Melodies from the minor pentatonic or harmonic minor (the raised 7th sounds dark)
Keep it simple: the melody loop repeats through the song
arrangement: Intro 4-8 bars (melody alone)
Hook 8 bars - Verse 16 bars - Hook 8 bars
Strip the drums in the intro and bridge; bring the full 808 in with the hook
mix: 808 in mono, under 100 Hz; saturate it for upper harmonics
Kick and 808 hit together (or sidechain the 808 to the kick)
Bright hats panned a little; reverb on the melody, the 808 dry
tips: Tune the 808 to the key: its pitch IS the bass line
Keep the melody high and sparse so the vocal has room

rnb.summary: R&B is smooth and soulful: rich chords, a warm bass that grooves, and drums that sit back so the voice can float.
rnb.feel: 4/4 with a laid-back, swung 16th feel; snare on 2 and 4, a little behind the beat.
rnb.keys: Major and minor keys with lots of 7th, 9th and 11th chords. Dorian minor is common.
sounds: Rhodes or another electric piano, warm keys
Smooth synth bass or fingered electric bass
Soft, punchy drums: rimshots, finger snaps, a tight kick
Pads, strings and lush vocal stacks
Chorused guitar licks; a talkbox in funkier styles
drums: Snare, rim or snap on 2 and 4, laid back
Kick syncopated around the bass line
16th hats with swing and a few skipped notes
Ghost notes and a shaker keep it moving
bass: Melodic: the root on the downbeat, then passing notes into the next chord
Slides and short syncopated notes; leave space
harmony: Extended chords: maj7, m7, 9ths, e.g. IVmaj7 - iii7 - ii7 - Imaj7
ii - V movements and chromatic passing chords
Move every note of a chord as little as possible to the next one (voice leading)
arrangement: Intro 4 - Verse 8 or 16 - Pre-chorus 4 - Chorus 8 - Bridge 8
Thin the drums in the verse; add pads and harmonies in the chorus
mix: Warm low mids, soft highs: nothing harsh
Kick and bass tight; vocal forward with a plate reverb and delay throws
tips: Let the keys answer the vocal with little rhythmic fills
Stack harmonies in the chorus

pop.summary: Pop is about the hook: a clear, catchy melody, simple strong chords and a polished production where every part lifts the chorus.
pop.feel: 4/4, straight. Kick on every beat (dance pop) or on 1 and 3, with the snare and a clap on 2 and 4.
pop.keys: Mostly major keys; minor for darker pop. Keep the melody in an easy singing range.
sounds: Punchy, clean drums with a clap layered on the snare
Synth bass or electric bass locked to the kick
Plucks, arpeggios and pads for movement and width
Vocal chops and ear candy (risers, sweeps)
drums: Kick on 1 and 3 (or every beat), snare and clap on 2 and 4
8th or 16th hats; open hats on the offbeats to lift the chorus
Build into the chorus with a snare roll or a riser
bass: Root notes in 8ths that follow the kick
Octave jumps add energy in the chorus
harmony: The four-chord loop: I - V - vi - IV (or vi - IV - I - V)
Keep the chords simple so the melody stands out
Change the bass note under a chord (an inversion) for a lift without new chords
arrangement: Intro 4-8 - Verse 8 - Pre-chorus 4-8 - Chorus 8 - Verse - Pre - Chorus - Bridge 8 - Final chorus
Each chorus adds something: a layer, a harmony, a drum change
mix: Bright and loud, the vocal on top
Sidechain pads and bass to the kick for a gentle pump
Wide chorus, narrower verse
tips: Write the chorus hook first, and repeat it
Contrast: the verse lower and sparser, the chorus higher and fuller

rock.summary: Rock is driven by guitars and a live band: big riffs and power chords, a pounding kit and a bass that locks the groove.
rock.feel: 4/4, straight 8ths; the snare hits hard on 2 and 4.
rock.keys: Guitar keys (E, A, D, G); major and minor, blues notes, and the flat 7 (Mixolydian).
sounds: Distorted electric guitars for the rhythm, plus a lead guitar
A live acoustic kit with room sound
Electric bass (played with a pick for punch)
Organ or piano in classic rock
Big cymbals: a crash on the first beat of each section
drums: Kick on 1 and 3 (and the 'and' of 3)
Snare on 2 and 4, loud
8ths on the hi-hat in the verse, on the ride or crash in the chorus
Tom fills at the ends of phrases
bass: Root 8th notes with the guitar riff
Follow the kick; walk up into the next chord
harmony: Power chords (root and fifth)
I - IV - V, I - bVII - IV, i - VI - VII
Riffs from the minor pentatonic
arrangement: Intro riff - Verse - Chorus - Verse - Chorus - Solo - Chorus
Double the guitars (left and right) in the chorus
mix: Guitars wide (two takes panned), bass and kick in the centre
Room mics on the drums for size
tips: Start with a riff, then fit the chords around it
Dynamics: a quieter verse makes a louder chorus

country.summary: Country tells a story: a clear vocal, acoustic and twangy electric guitars, steel or fiddle fills, and a solid, simple groove.
country.feel: 4/4, straight or with a shuffle; a two-beat or train beat in classic country.
country.keys: Major keys (G, D, A, E, C: guitar keys, often with a capo).
sounds: A twangy electric (Telecaster style) with slapback delay
Pedal steel, fiddle, banjo or dobro for fills
Live drums and a round electric bass
drums: Kick on 1 and 3, snare on 2 and 4 (modern)
A two-beat or train beat (snare 8ths with accents) in classic styles
Brushes for ballads and Americana
bass: Root on 1, fifth on 3 (the 'boom-chick')
Walk up or down into the next chord
harmony: I - IV - V and I - V - vi - IV
The II major chord and the vi minor for a lift
Simple chords: the story and the melody matter most
arrangement: Intro lick - Verse - Chorus - Verse - Chorus - Bridge or solo - Chorus
Steel or fiddle fills answer the vocal lines
mix: The vocal clear and upfront
Bright acoustic; the electric with slapback
Natural, roomy reverb
tips: Fill the gaps between vocal lines with a lick
Keep the beat steady and simple

worship.summary: Worship music builds: ambient pads and piano under a singable melody, growing from a quiet start to a big, anthemic chorus.
worship.feel: 4/4 (sometimes 6/8). It builds from sparse to full; delay guitars give an 8th-note pulse.
worship.keys: Singable major keys: G, A, B, C, D, E.
sounds: Ambient pads (shimmer, swells) holding the song up
Clean electric guitars with a dotted-8th delay, and swells
Warm bass, with a deep sub in the builds
Big live drums with toms; choir and strings in the bridge
drums: Verse: kick on 1, a rim or nothing else
Build: toms and 8th-note kicks
Chorus: kick on 1 and 3, snare on 2 and 4, crashes
Cymbal swells into the big sections
bass: Whole and half notes on the roots; octaves in the chorus
An 8th-note pulse in the builds
harmony: I - V - vi - IV, IV - I - V - vi, vi - IV - I - V
Sus2 and add9 chords for an open sound
The bridge often starts on IV or vi
arrangement: Intro (pad and piano) - Verse - Chorus - Verse - Chorus - Bridge (repeated, building) - Chorus - Tag
Dynamics are everything: drop to the pad alone, then build
mix: Long reverbs and delays
Pads wide and low in level
The vocal clear and centred
tips: A dotted-8th delay on the guitar gives that shimmer
Let the bridge repeat and build two or three times

edm.summary: EDM is built for the dance floor: a driving kick, big builds and drops, and sound design that keeps moving.
edm.feel: 4/4 with the kick on every beat (house, techno); half time for dubstep; breakbeats for drum & bass.
edm.keys: Mostly minor keys (F, G, A minor) with simple chords.
sounds: A punchy kick with a tight low end
Synth bass (a sub plus a mid layer), plucks, supersaw chords
Risers, sweeps and impacts for builds and drops
drums: Kick on every beat
Clap on 2 and 4
Open hat on every offbeat; 16th closed hats for drive
A snare roll that speeds up into the drop
bass: Offbeat bass (between the kicks) in house
Rolling 16ths or a sustained sub elsewhere
harmony: i - VI - III - VII, vi - IV - I - V
Stab chords on the offbeats
Keep the bass and chords simple: the groove matters most
arrangement: Intro 16-32 bars (DJ friendly) - Build 8-16 - Drop 16-32 - Break - Build - Drop - Outro
Take the kick out in the breakdown; bring it back at the drop
mix: Sidechain almost everything to the kick
Mono below 120 Hz
Loud and bright; automate filters in the builds
tips: Make the drop simple and strong
Movement comes from automation (filters, volume, effects)

lofi.summary: Lo-fi is relaxed and nostalgic: dusty swung drums, jazzy chords, a soft bass and a warm, worn tape sound.
lofi.feel: 4/4 with heavy swing; the drums lazy, a little behind the beat.
lofi.keys: Minor and major with jazz chords: maj7, m7, m9.
sounds: Rhodes, felt piano or jazz guitar chords
A warm round bass or upright
Vinyl crackle, tape hiss, rain or room ambience
A mellow lead: flute, muted trumpet, guitar
drums: A boom-bap pattern with lots of swing
A soft snare or rim on 2 and 4
Hats lazy and quiet; skip a few
bass: Round notes on the roots with a few passing notes
Leave space: less is more
harmony: ii7 - V7 - Imaj7 - vi7 and IVmaj7 - iii7 - vi7
Add 9ths; a little detune (wow and flutter) adds age
arrangement: Short loops (8-16 bars) that change slowly
Filter the drums in and out
mix: Low-pass everything a little and roll off the highs
Tape saturation and wobble
Quiet and warm, not loud
tips: Imperfect is good: swing, wobble, crackle
Keep it short (under three minutes)

cinematic.summary: Cinematic music paints a picture: big strings and brass, epic percussion, and dramatic builds that follow the story.
cinematic.tempo: Free, or 60-140 BPM; tension builds speed up
cinematic.feel: 4/4 or 3/4. Ostinatos (short repeating patterns) drive the motion.
cinematic.keys: Minor keys for drama (D, C minor); modal colours (Dorian, Phrygian).
sounds: String ensemble: staccato ostinatos and long legato lines
Brass: horns for heroic lines, low brass for weight
Epic drums: taikos, toms, hits and booms
Piano for emotion, choir for size
drums: Taiko and tom patterns on 1 and 3 that build up
Big hits (booms) at the start of sections
Snare rolls for tension
bass: Low strings or brass on long root notes
Pedal tones: one low note under changing chords
harmony: i - VI - III - VII, i - iv - VI - V
Pedal points and suspended chords build tension
Minor to major at the end for triumph
arrangement: Start small (piano or pad) and add a layer every 8 bars
Build - climax - release; trailers often in three acts
mix: Big hall reverbs
Strings wide, percussion centred
tips: Ostinato strings keep the momentum
Contrast quiet and loud sections

hiphop.east.summary: East Coast boom bap: hard sampled drums, a chopped soul or jazz sample and a gritty, swung groove (think Nas, Gang Starr, Wu-Tang).
sounds: Dusty drum breaks sampled from records
Jazz or soul samples: piano, horns, strings
An upright or deep bass that follows the kick
tips: Chop the sample on the beat and re-order the pieces
Swing the hats, keep the kick and snare tight

hiphop.west.summary: West Coast G-funk: slow rolling grooves, a whiny high synth lead, funky bass and P-Funk style keys (think Dr. Dre, Snoop Dogg, Warren G).
sounds: A high synth lead that glides between notes (the G-funk whistle)
harmony: Minor 7th to a major-ish IV7 (Dorian): i7 - IV7
Smooth, laid-back chord changes
tips: Let the synth lead slide (portamento) between notes
Lay the bass back a little behind the beat

hiphop.memphis.summary: Memphis rap and phonk: dark and lo-fi, cowbell melodies, distorted 808s and chopped vocal samples (think Three 6 Mafia; phonk: Kordhell, DVRST).
hiphop.memphis.keys: Minor and Phrygian (the flat 2 sounds evil): i - bII
drums: Trap-style half time with a hard clap on 3
Fast hats with rolls
Cowbell patterns as the lead
tips: Distort the 808 hard and low-pass the vocal samples
Keep the melody short and repeating

hiphop.south.summary: Southern hip-hop and crunk: big 808 kicks, chanted hooks, synth stabs and slowed-down 'chopped and screwed' moods (think UGK, Three 6 Mafia, Lil Jon).
tips: Hooks are chanted: short, loud and repeated
Slow it down and pitch it down for the 'screwed' sound

hiphop.oldschool.summary: Old school and electro: drum machines (808, DMX), funky bass and breakbeats built for breakdancing (think Afrika Bambaataa, Run-DMC, Grandmaster Flash).
sounds: Roland TR-808 drums: cowbell, hand claps, toms
Synth bass and robot vocoder voices
tips: Program the drums stiff and electronic
Answer the rap with stabs and scratches

trap.atlanta.summary: Atlanta trap: hard 808s, rapid hats and dark piano or bell loops (think Metro Boomin, Southside, Future).

trap.ukdrill.summary: UK drill: sliding 808s, stop-start syncopated drums and dark minor melodies (think Headie One, Central Cee, M-Huncho).
trap.ukdrill.feel: Half time, with a snare on 3 and an extra, late snare; hats in triplet-ish patterns; the 808 slides between notes.
drums: Snare on beat 3 plus a late snare just before beat 4 in every other bar
Kicks syncopated, rarely on the downbeat after bar 1
Hats in triplet groups with gaps
bass: The 808 slides: overlap the notes so the glide plays
Move between the root, the fifth and the minor third

trap.nydrill.summary: NY drill: Brooklyn's take on UK drill, with sliding 808s, sampled vocal or R&B loops and aggressive drums (think Pop Smoke, Fivio Foreign).
sounds: Sampled vocal or R&B loops, choirs

trap.rage.summary: Rage: fast, loud and distorted, with buzzing supersaw leads, blown-out 808s and lots of energy (think Playboi Carti, Trippie Redd, Ken Carson).
tips: Distortion on almost everything; keep the parts few and loud
A simple four-note lead loop is enough

trap.plugg.summary: Plugg and melodic trap: soft, bright synths and pads, bouncy 808s and dreamy melodies (think Pi'erre Bourne, Lil Uzi Vert).
trap.plugg.keys: Major keys and major-7th chords are common here, unlike darker trap.
sounds: Bright, video-game style synth leads and plucks
harmony: Major 7th chords: Imaj7 - vi7 - IVmaj7 - V
Sweet, simple melodies

rnb.newjack.summary: New jack swing and 90s R&B: swung hip-hop drums with R&B chords and harmonies, synth stabs and gated snares (think Teddy Riley, Bobby Brown, Boyz II Men).
sounds: Gated, punchy snares and hard claps

rnb.neosoul.summary: Neo soul: live-feeling, jazzy chords, laid-back drums and a warm bass (think D'Angelo, Erykah Badu, Jill Scott).
harmony: Chords that move by step with 9ths and 11ths: i9 - iv9, IVmaj7 - iii7 - ii7 - Imaj7
Play the drums and bass slightly late for that lazy pocket

rnb.alt.summary: Modern and alternative R&B: dark, spacious and trap-influenced, with moody pads and lots of reverb (think The Weeknd, Frank Ocean, SZA, Bryson Tiller).
sounds: Sparse trap drums with soft hats

rnb.funk.summary: Funk and Motown: tight live band grooves, syncopated bass, horn stabs and everything landing on 'the one' (think James Brown, Stevie Wonder, The Temptations).
sounds: Slap or fingered bass full of syncopation
Tight live drums with ghost notes
drums: Hit 'the one' hard; ghost notes on the snare
16th hats, open on some offbeats

pop.synth.summary: Synth pop and the 80s: gated drums, analog synths, arpeggios and big chorus melodies (think a-ha, Depeche Mode, The Weeknd's 'Blinding Lights').
sounds: Analog poly synths (Juno, Jupiter) and arpeggios

pop.dance.summary: Dance pop: four-on-the-floor, sidechained chords and a huge hook (think Dua Lipa, Lady Gaga, Calvin Harris).

pop.rock.summary: Pop rock: guitars and live drums with pop melodies and polish (think Paramore, Kelly Clarkson, Maroon 5).
sounds: Crunchy electric guitars with clean pop production

pop.indie.summary: Indie and bedroom pop: lo-fi warmth, dreamy chorused guitars, soft synths and an intimate vocal (think Clairo, Rex Orange County, beabadoobee).
sounds: A simple drum machine or loose live drums
harmony: Major 7ths: Imaj7 - vi7 - IVmaj7 - V
Gentle, dreamy changes

rock.classic.summary: Classic rock: blues-based riffs, Hammond organ and live band energy (think Led Zeppelin, The Rolling Stones, Lynyrd Skynyrd).
sounds: Live drums in a big room

rock.hard.summary: Hard rock: heavier riffs, louder guitars and big choruses (think AC/DC, Guns N' Roses, Foo Fighters).

rock.metal.summary: Metal: down-tuned, high-gain guitars, double-kick drums and palm-muted riffs (think Metallica, Slipknot, Bring Me the Horizon).
rock.metal.keys: E, D and C minor; drop tunings; Phrygian (flat 2) for darkness.
drums: Double kick in 16ths under the riff
Snare on 2 and 4 (or half time)
China and crash cymbals

rock.alt.summary: Alternative and grunge: quiet-loud dynamics, fuzzy guitars and moody chords (think Nirvana, Radiohead, Pearl Jam).
harmony: Moody minor progressions and unexpected major chords
Quiet verse, explosive chorus on the same chords

rock.punk.summary: Punk and pop punk: fast, simple and loud, with power chords, driving 8ths and shout-along choruses (think Ramones, Green Day, Blink-182).
drums: The skate beat: kick on the beat, snare on every offbeat
Crash on every chorus downbeat

country.classic.summary: Classic country and honky-tonk: a shuffle or two-beat, steel guitar and fiddle, honky-tonk piano (think Hank Williams, George Strait, Merle Haggard).

country.modern.summary: Modern Nashville: pop-polished country with big choruses, loops and a live band (think Morgan Wallen, Luke Combs, Kane Brown).
sounds: A clean electric with delay; banjo loops
A sub or 808 layered under the bass

country.rap.summary: Country rap: trap drums and an 808 under country guitars and storytelling (think Jelly Roll, Upchurch, Colt Ford).
sounds: Trap drums with an 808 in the kit
A bass that sits above the 808
bass: The 808 goes with the drums; the bass guitar plays above it (or follows the same notes)

country.americana.summary: Americana and folk: acoustic, organic and rootsy, with acoustic guitar, banjo, mandolin and upright bass (think Chris Stapleton, Zach Bryan, The Lumineers).
sounds: Stomps, claps and a sparse kit
drums: Kick 'stomp' on 1 and 3, claps or snare on 2 and 4
Brushes and tambourine

worship.modern.summary: Modern worship: big builds, ambient guitars and pads and anthemic choruses (think Elevation Worship, Hillsong, Bethel).

worship.gospel.summary: Gospel and church: Hammond organ, piano runs, a choir and tight drums with fills, over rich, soulful harmony (think Kirk Franklin, Tye Tribbett, Maverick City).
sounds: Hammond organ with a Leslie speaker
Gospel piano with runs and fills
Tight drums with chops and ghost notes
harmony: Lots of 7ths and passing chords: ii7 - V7 - Imaj7
The IV - iv change (major to minor four) for emotion
Walk-ups between chords

worship.ambient.summary: Ambient worship and hymns: spacious pads, piano and soft swells, with little or no drums.
drums: Often no drums; a soft kick on 1 or swells
Bring in toms only for the climax

edm.house.summary: House: four-on-the-floor at 120-128 BPM, offbeat hats, a groovy bass and piano or organ stabs (think Disclosure, Fisher, Frankie Knuckles).

edm.techno.summary: Techno: hypnotic, driving and minimal at 125-140 BPM, with dark synths and lots of percussion (think Charlotte de Witte, Adam Beyer, Amelie Lens).
harmony: Often one chord or none: the groove and the sound are the music
A short, repeating synth motif that changes slowly

edm.dnb.summary: Drum & bass: fast breakbeats at 170-175 BPM with a deep sub bass and rolling energy (think Pendulum, Chase & Status, Netsky).
edm.dnb.feel: The two-step: kick on 1 and the 'and' of 3, snare on 2 and 4, at high speed.

edm.dubstep.summary: Dubstep and bass music: half time at 140 BPM with huge, wobbling basses and big drops (think Skrillex, Excision).
edm.dubstep.feel: Half time: kick on 1, snare on 3.

edm.disco.summary: Disco and nu-disco: four-on-the-floor, octave bass lines, strings and funky guitars (think Daft Punk, Purple Disco Machine, Dua Lipa's 'Levitating').

lofi.jazzhop.summary: Jazz hop and chillhop: swung boom-bap drums with jazz chords and samples (think Nujabes, J Dilla, the Lofi Girl playlists).

lofi.trap.summary: Lo-fi trap and sad trap: slow, emotional trap with lo-fi textures, soft 808s, sad piano and guitar (think XXXTentacion, Juice WRLD's mellow songs).
sounds: Sad piano or clean guitar loops

cinematic.trailer.summary: Epic trailer music: a three-act build with big drums, brass and choir, rising tension and huge hits (think Two Steps From Hell, Hans Zimmer).

cinematic.horror.summary: Dark and horror: dissonance, drones, sudden hits and silence (think the 'Hereditary' score, 'Stranger Things' synths).
cinematic.horror.keys: Minor and Phrygian; clusters and the flat 2.
harmony: Phrygian: i - bII
Hold a low drone and move dissonant notes above it

cinematic.world.summary: World percussion: rhythmic ensembles of hand drums, frame drums and ethnic percussion over drones (think 'The Lion King', 'Gladiator').
sounds: Hand drums, frame drums, djembe, congas
Drones and ethnic flutes or voices
